name: Herman Moll, A New & Exact Map of the Coast, Countries and Islands within ye Limits of ye South Sea Company, 1711, inset 'Peypses or Pepys I.'
holding: David Rumsey Map Collection, list no. 9729.014, via the Internet Archive and Wikimedia Commons
note: 7942x8441. The inset is the drawing from Cowley's voyage that Moll had already engraved for William Hacke's Collection of Original Voyages (1699, plate facing p. 6): a bird's-eye view of two islands, Mount Charles and Peyps's Tableland on the north-western one, Mount James on the south-eastern, with Admiralty Bay running between them, and Catherine, George, Ann, Mary and Secretaries Points named. Chosen by Etienne in November 2026 over Hacke's 1699 printing, which survives here only as a black-and-white microfilm (EEBO, via the Internet Archive) that fills the hachures solid and cuts off the east end. Parker (BJHS 51, 2018) describes Hacke's 1687 manuscript roll (BL Add MS 17940B) as the same two islands with a strait; it was not seen.
extraction_note: --mode blue --bright (yellow): the colourist washed a yellow band along every coast, so the wash's outer edge is the shore where no coast line is engraved (the north-east flanks), and the engraved line where it is (the south shore, whose sea shading falls outside the mask). The same wash runs straight across Admiralty Bay, so the channel is cut back out with --channel (the unhatched pixels between the two islands) after the 'Bay' lettering across it is painted out; its north-east outlet, crowded to 25 px by the end of a coast line and a tree symbol, is opened with a hand-drawn --cut. Two parts. Moll draws a line marked S.E. and, upside down, N.W. beside the island; it is not read as a compass, since north-up agrees with Cowley's harbour 'on the SW coast'.
graticule_note: The main map is a Mercator sheet with 10-degree lines: meridians 70 and 60 W at x 4501 and 4903 (40.2 px per degree), parallels 40 and 50 S at y 6628 and 7204 near Patagonia. Its longitudes are about 5 degrees west of the truth along that coast (Cabo Blanco, 65.75 W, is drawn at 70.9 W), so Pepys Isle is placed by its offset from the coast Moll draws, not by his longitude.
